thesis: August 5 was an entry-quality and stop-loss failure: all 5 positions lost, producing INR -1,414.09 gross, INR 242.81 in charges, and INR -1,656.90 net. PNBHOUSING's Top Gainer Pullback emergency stop lost INR 690.71, three Breakdown positions lost INR 663.81, and one Rangebound position lost INR 302.38. Those setups have too little multi-date evidence for a defensible disable or threshold change. The older recurring Momentum Runner loss remains actionable, while Rangebound cost filtering remains only a low-confidence research change.

selectedDay.exitSummary: Three Stop exits lost INR 1,292.16 net, one Time / No progress exit lost INR 216.38, and the EOD exit lost INR 148.36. Stored day-close benchmarks cover all exits but do not establish an executable alternative.

limitations: This is analytics-reviewed only. No Replay, backtest, sweep, or targeted settings trial was run.
August 5 has 191 snapshots, 187 usable snapshots, and one settings fingerprint. Repeated snapshot appearances were not treated as independent observations.
Breakdown has only 4 positions across 2 dates in this window, and Top Gainer Pullback has only 3 positions across 3 dates; that is insufficient for enable or threshold changes.
Transactions do not store the entry-time expected gross-to-cost multiple, so the exact trades affected by tightening the Rangebound cost gate cannot be identified.
Day-close opportunity values are hindsight benchmarks and cannot prove a later executable exit.

topGainerSelectionAnalysis.conclusion: Top-gainer rank did not grant automatic selection. No captured top-five rejection was caused by cash, capacity, max-open, cooldown, or trade-limit controls. The dominant blockers were the falling Nifty regime, score floors, unconfirmed triggers, disabled CHASING classification, excessive extension or faded impulse, and late cutoffs.

otherPersistentCandidates.outcome: Not opened despite a 93.55 Top Gainer Pullback score because Nifty was down 0.986%.
Opened as TOP_GAINER_PULLBACK_RECLAIM at 10:41 IST and later lost INR 690.71. It is not a missed selection.

topGainerSelectionAnalysis.dataCaveat: PNBHOUSING opened between adjacent snapshots: the row 20 seconds before entry still showed a Nifty-regime rejection and the row 101 seconds after entry showed no rejection. The exact live admission transition is not persisted as an entry intent.

recommendations.description: Allows Momentum Runner candidates to open new simulation trades.
recommendations.rationale: Pause new Momentum Runner entries because the setup remains strongly negative across the most recent dates that contain its transactions.
evidence: Affected group: all 19 Momentum Runner positions across 5 dates; 4 wins, INR -3,005.65 gross, INR 1,211.94 charges, INR -4,217.59 net, INR -221.98 expectancy, and profit factor 0.15.
Unaffected group: 60 other positions; INR 2,487.71 gross, INR 3,907.75 charges, and INR -1,420.04 net.
Four dates support pausing: July 28, July 29, July 31, and August 3. July 30 contradicts with INR 138.20 net; August 4 and August 5 have no Momentum Runner transaction evidence.
The affected setup is negative on 4 of 5 dates containing relevant transactions, or 80%.
recommendations.risk: Pausing removes the profitable July 30 subgroup and any future recovery. It would not have prevented August 5's losses because no Momentum Runner position closed that day.

validation.reason: Medium confidence: aggregate evidence and 80% date support are favorable, but 19 affected transactions fall one short of the high-confidence minimum of 20. This was not replay-tested or validated.

recommendations.description: Minimum rangebound gross move as a multiple of modeled costs.
recommendations.rationale: Research aligning the Rangebound-specific cost hurdle with the shared 2.5 multiple because recent gross gains have not covered charges, but preserve 2.0 until the exact entry-time affected group is observable.
evidence: Relevant setup population: 27 Rangebound positions across 4 dates; 9 wins, INR 906.73 gross, INR 1,393.26 charges, INR -486.53 net, INR -18.02 expectancy, and profit factor 0.85.
Three relevant dates support a stricter cost hurdle: August 3, August 4, and August 5. July 31 contradicts with INR 378.90 net; three window dates have no Rangebound transactions.

August 4 was the clearest cost-drag example: INR 74.24 gross became INR -487.14 after charges. August 5's single Rangebound loss was gross-negative and would not necessarily be prevented by a cost filter.
Seven Target exits earned INR 2,397.96 net, while seven Stop exits lost INR 2,184.62; a higher entry cost hurdle cannot substitute for stop-quality work.
recommendations.risk: The expected gross-to-cost multiple at entry is absent from stored transactions, so the exact affected count is unknown. Tightening may reject profitable trades and would not address the observed emergency or confirmed-stop failures directly.

validation.reason: Low confidence because the exact 2.0-to-2.5 affected population is not measurable even though 27 relevant trades across 4 dates show aggregate cost drag. Preserve the current value pending direct mechanism evidence.
